rounds.note: Round 1 fixes all six findings in a single concurrent wave, none touching production code: the blocker (#0) is an oracle defect, not a copy defect — the honest quiet-hours negation stays and T4 is re-pointed at the actual B160 claim (old sentence absent, "not yet held or delayed" present), with its stale comment corrected in the same edit (#4). Test-strength gaps are closed by pinning the production NO_TRANSPORT matrix shape and setRuleEnabled rejection against a transports-false provider in a second module (#1), adding the LOW_STOCK negative control to the T5 scanner harness (#2), and asserting the seeded enabled/disabled rows in REG-B182 T7 (#3). The build-plan artifact's NotificationsSettingsTab path gains its missing _components/ segment (#5). Both web gates (red gate `-t "REG-B(160|180)"` and `npx jest --silent`) plus the api messaging suites must be green after the wave; no map/lessons/ledger edits per Option B.

Round 2 has a single minor finding: the NO_TRANSPORT test's "leaves INTERNAL untouched" assertion is vacuous because every INTERNAL event is a NO_TRIGGER event, so the `channel !== INTERNAL` exemption is unreachable and the assertion passes on precedence alone (proven by the reviewer's mutation probe). Plan: one wave, one Sonnet executor — drop the vacuous assertion, retitle the test to claim only what it proves, and pin the actual current state behaviorally (every INTERNAL cell in getMatrix under the no-transport provider reports NO_TRIGGER) so the first wired INTERNAL event turns the test red and forces a real exemption test; add a comment-only note at the service check recording the exemption as currently unreachable and kept for the first wired INTERNAL event. No production logic, constants, or existing EMAIL/setRuleEnabled assertions change; Option-B bookkeeping (no map/lessons/ledger edits) respected.

issues.issue: The pin test "toggles a rule's enabled flag" (lines 181-198) calls setRuleEnabled on a NotificationEvent.DELIVERED / MessageChannel.PORTAL rule and asserts the update resolves with enabled:true. Per cause-ruling.md §2, PORTAL has no capability-seam transport (StubProvider declares no transports for PORTAL, per T2 in bug-test-plan.md), so under P2's rule that setRuleEnabled refuses any 'unavailable' cell (NO_TRANSPORT included) with BadRequestException, this fixture's channel becomes unavailable and the call will now throw instead of resolving with the update mock. The test plan's harness notes only flag the LOW_STOCK/NO_TRIGGER rewrite (T6) and the WHATSAPP consent-writer case (T8); this PORTAL-based pin is not covered and will fail once P2 lands.
issues.remedy: Change this pin's fixture channel to one with a real transport (e.g. EMAIL or another channel StubProvider declares), or explicitly add it as a T6/T8-style case if PORTAL enabling must remain rejected.

confirmedFindings.summary: The config-side NO_TRANSPORT branch — the one that fires for every non-INTERNAL cell in production — is never executed by any test, because the only spec that constructs MessagingConfigService hard-codes `transports() === true` and never overrides it.
confirmedFindings.detail: `provider = { send: jest.fn(), transports: jest.fn().mockReturnValue(true) }` is set once in beforeEach; `grep -n transports messaging-config.service.spec.ts` returns exactly 2 hits (the type and this line), and `grep -rln MessagingConfigService apps/api/src --include=*.spec.ts` returns only this file. So `unavailabilityReason`'s `if (channel !== INTERNAL && !this.provider.transports(channel)) return "NO_TRANSPORT"` can never be taken in any test. Failure scenario: delete that line from messaging-config.service.ts and the entire api suite still passes (the send-side check is a separate line in messaging.service.ts, covered by messaging.transport-honesty.spec.ts) — yet the settings matrix would again render live enable switches for EMAIL/PORTAL/WA/SMS cells that the engine will always skip with NO_TRANSPORT, which is the exact B180/B183 user-visible shape this change exists to remove. Second consequence of the same mock: with the production StubProvider declaring no transports, `unavailabilityReason` returns NO_TRANSPORT before ever reaching the `requiresConsent` branch, so the value REG-B183 T8 pins (`unavailable === "NO_CONSENT_WRITER"`, spec line ~299) is unreachable in production today — that assertion holds only under the always-true mock.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Add a case that binds a provider declaring `transports: () => false` (or the real StubProvider) and asserts a customer-channel cell comes back `{ unavailable: "NO_TRANSPORT", enabled: false }` and that setRuleEnabled rejects it — i.e. pin the matrix shape the deployed system actually serves; keep the always-true provider for T6/T8 so the NO_TRIGGER / NO_CONSENT_WRITER precedence stays covered.

confirmedFindings.summary: The T5 static guard has a positive control but no negative control: `hasFiringSite` is only ever asserted true, so a scanner that always reports "wired" would keep the guard permanently green.
confirmedFindings.detail: Both harness-integrity pins (line 62 file count, line 66 `hasFiringSite("OUT_FOR_DELIVERY") === true`) and the REG-B180 assertion (line 76, `unwired` is empty) pass whenever `hasFiringSite` returns true. Failure scenario: someone removes or breaks the `if (full === MESSAGING_DIR) continue` skip at line 32 (e.g. while re-rooting the walk). messaging-config.service.ts then enters SOURCES and it textually contains `NotificationEvent.OUT_FOR_DELIVERY`, `NotificationEvent.LOW_STOCK`, etc. in EVENT_CHANNELS/DEFAULT_TEMPLATES/NO_TRIGGER_EVENTS, so every key reports a firing site, the guard stays green forever, and a future unwired key re-added to DEFAULT_ON ships silently — precisely the B180 regression the spec is meant to block. A negative control is available for free and true today: I confirmed by grep that `NotificationEvent.LOW_STOCK` / `URGENT_ORDER_PLACED` / `FAILED_DELIVERY` / `PAYMENT_FAILED_NSF` have zero references in apps/api/src outside messaging/ and outside *.spec.ts.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Add one pin next to line 66: `expect(hasFiringSite("LOW_STOCK")).toBe(false)` (with a comment that it is the scanner's negative control, to be re-pointed at another unwired key if LOW_STOCK ever gains a trigger).

confirmedFindings.summary: REG-B182 T7 never asserts what was seeded, so a seeder that dropped the DEFAULT_ON semantics (everything seeded disabled) would still pass.
confirmedFindings.detail: The test asserts only `createMany` call count and `toMatchObject({ skipDuplicates: true })` on the args, then asserts `outcomes[0]` is `{channel: "EMAIL", outcome: "sent"}` — but that outcome comes entirely from the hard-coded second mock (`notificationRule.findMany ... .mockResolvedValue([{ channel: MessageChannel.EMAIL }])`), not from the seed, so the dispatch half of the assertion is the mock testing itself. Failure scenario: change `seedDefaultsFor` to push `{ eventKey, channel, enabled: false }` unconditionally (dropping DEFAULT_ON) — B182's documented outcome ("INVOICE_SENT:EMAIL is on by default for a never-visited tenant") is destroyed, and T7 plus the whole api suite stay green. The seeded payload is observable: `createMany.mock.calls[0][0].data` is the full rule array.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Extend the existing args assertion to check the seeded rows, e.g. `expect(createMany.mock.calls[0][0].data).toContainEqual({ eventKey: NotificationEvent.INVOICE_SENT, channel: MessageChannel.EMAIL, enabled: true })` and one `enabled: false` counterpart (e.g. ORDER_CONFIRMED:WHATSAPP).

confirmedFindings.summary: The T4 test's own comment states a requirement the system does not implement — that quiet-hours messages are "queued for the next send window".
confirmedFindings.detail: Lines 68-69 read "quiet hours are recorded (queued for the next send window), never held indefinitely". Nothing queues: messaging.service.ts:129-135 computes `wouldBeQuiet` and the value is only echoed on the outcome; cause-ruling.md §2 explicitly defers the hold queue as a feature, and the copy this test guards says "not yet held or delayed". Failure scenario: a later reader trusts the comment and restores a scheduling claim in the card copy (the exact B160 wording bug), and the test — whose oracle is a substring, not the claim — will not necessarily object. Since the assertion on line 75 has to be reworked anyway (finding 1), the comment should be corrected in the same edit.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Reword to state the actual contract: the window is recorded on the send outcome only; nothing is held, delayed, or queued in P6-2.

confirmedFindings.summary: NotificationsSettingsTab.tsx path is incomplete — missing _components/ subdirectory
confirmedFindings.detail: In build-plan.md: The artifact claims the file is at `apps/web/app/(dashboard)/settings/NotificationsSettingsTab.tsx`, but the actual file is located at `apps/web/app/(dashboard)/settings/_components/NotificationsSettingsTab.tsx`. The path in the artifact omits the _components directory level.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Update the path in P4 from `apps/web/app/(dashboard)/settings/NotificationsSettingsTab.tsx` to `apps/web/app/(dashboard)/settings/_components/NotificationsSettingsTab.tsx`
